invariant: Every refused oversized event-batch upload receives its governed 413 BATCH_FRAMING_REFUSED response; mid-stream refusal followed by body drain must leave the connection usable for subsequent requests.
reproduction: Unskip the single it block in tests/rfl-oversize-upload-connection.test.ts, then run: npm run test:integration -- tests/rfl-oversize-upload-connection.test.ts
paths: src/governance-service/GovernanceHttpService.ts (ingestBatch framing, readIncomingBody size refusal, post-refusal resume drain)
src/governance-service/server-entry.ts (combined server without timeout envelope; contrast createGovernanceHttpServer)
observed: Refused multi-MB uploads intermittently receive a transport error (ECONNRESET via undici keep-alive reuse) instead of the governed 413: 2.4MB bodies 4/10 failures, 5.1MB bodies 4/10 failures across consecutive runs, 2.05MB bodies 0/10. Empty and small requests always receive governed responses. Service stays healthy throughout; rate limiting unaffected. Prime suspect (hypothesis, not established): the post-refusal resume() drain races the client's still-transmitting upload and the socket is destroyed, poisoning the pooled connection for the next request that draws it.
notes: RFL recorded only; no production code changed. Skipped reproducer committed alongside for independent rerun after any transport fix.
